messages.subject: [statnet_help] Nodematch in Statnet
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
? ? I'm having repeated difficulties with the models in statnet, specifically with nodematch. ?
? ? I have a weighted, undirected, unipartite network that I'm trying to analyze. ? I've tried two separate methods: In the first method, I read in the network from a .net file. It keeps the edge weight, but strips all of the node attributes. ?In general, everything works well with this method: triangles, mean degree, kstar(x) all work, even if they don't always converge. ?However, I can't bring through any vertex attributes. ?Pajek strips them away. ?One of those attributes, region, is vital to my analysis. ?I can re-add the attributes to a graph based on the matrix of my network, but 'nodematch' gets confused and says that the vertex attributes do not exist. ?I've checked the graph object to make sure that the vertex attributes were added correctly, and they are there. ?I can and have used them in plots.
? ? Subsequently, if I build the network using the 'network' module from an edgelist, I can keep the vertex attributes, but I lose the ability to give the network a weight. ?When I run Summary on the network constructed this way, all of the node attributes ARE listed. ?However, when I indicate that directed = FALSE, it doesn't register for some reason, which makes the kstar(x) in statnet give an error (it will allow istar, even though I tell it directed = FALSE). ?And, when I run ERGM with nodematch or mutual, statnet tells me that the attribute 'region' doesn't exist, even though (as I said earlier) that field is specifically mentioned as a vertex attribute.
? ? ?Are these known issues with workarounds?
Thanks for any help you can provide. :-)
Jess

rburke@cs.depaul.edu


From: Jess Behrens <jess_behrens03@yahoo.com>
Reply-To: Jess Behrens <jess_behrens03@yahoo.com>
Date: Thursday, June 8, 2017 at 6:45 AM
To: "statnet_help@u.washington.edu" <statnet_help@u.washington.edu>
Subject: [statnet_help] Nodematch in Statnet

Hi,

    I'm having repeated difficulties with the models in statnet, specifically with nodematch.

    I have a weighted, undirected, unipartite network that I'm trying to analyze.   I've tried two separate methods: In the first method, I read in the network from a .net file. It keeps the edge weight, but strips all of the node attributes.  In general, everything works well with this method: triangles, mean degree, kstar(x) all work, even if they don't always converge.  However, I can't bring through any vertex attributes.  Pajek strips them away.  One of those attributes, region, is vital to my analysis.  I can re-add the attributes to a graph based on the matrix of my network, but 'nodematch' gets confused and says that the vertex attributes do not exist.  I've checked the graph object to make sure that the vertex attributes were added correctly, and they are there.  I can and have used them in plots.

    Subsequently, if I build the network using the 'network' module from an edgelist, I can keep the vertex attributes, but I lose the ability to give the network a weight.  When I run Summary on the network constructed this way, all of the node attributes ARE listed.  However, when I indicate that directed = FALSE, it doesn't register for some reason, which makes the kstar(x) in statnet give an error (it will allow istar, even though I tell it directed = FALSE).  And, when I run ERGM with nodematch or mutual, statnet tells me that the attribute 'region' doesn't exist, even though (as I said earlier) that field is specifically mentioned as a vertex attribute.

     Are these known issues with workarounds?

Thanks for any help you can provide. :-)

Jess

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Weird summary behavior after loading the "network" package
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] Weird summary behavior after loading the "network" package
messages.body_plain:
Dear statnet list,

	I have been having a weird bug lately when calling summary
on data frames containing character columns, and it seems to be
related to the network package.

The following code is sufficient to reproduce the bug, after calling

R --no-restore

---
test <- data.frame(a=c("some", "char", "vector", "with", "many", 
"many", "words"), b=1:7, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
summary(test)
summary(test$a)
library("network")
summary(test)
summary(test$a)
---

The output for the first summary(test) is:

       a                   b
  Length:7           Min.   :1.0
  Class :character   1st Qu.:2.5
  Mode  :character   Median :4.0
                     Mean   :4.0
                     3rd Qu.:5.5
                     Max.   :7.0

as expected, while the same command after loading network gives:

     a                b
  NULL:some     Min.   :1.0
  NULL:char     1st Qu.:2.5
  NULL:vector   Median :4.0
  NULL:with     Mean   :4.0
  NULL:many     3rd Qu.:5.5
  NULL:many     Max.   :7.0
  NULL:words

Notice the repetition: *every* line is printed, prepended by "NULL:", 
and it becomes impossible to read when there are thousands of lines.

In both cases, summary(test$a) gives the expected output.

The prepended NULL comes from these three lines in summary.data.frame:

         sms <- format(sms, digits = digits)
         lbs <- format(names(sms))
         sms <- paste0(lbs, ":", sms, "  ")

It's inside a for loop over columns, where sms is the output of summary 
for the current column. For character columns, names(sms) is NULL, hence 
the issue.

I'm on R version 3.3.3 (2017-03-06), using network
Version 1.13.0 created on 2015-08-31. I'll be happy to upgrade if
this is a known bug.

Thanks a lot for your help!

Matteo

messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] Weird summary behavior after loading the "network" package
messages.body_plain:
Hello Carter,

    that is exaclty the issue: loading network changes the behavior of 
UseMethod("summary") globally for character vectors.

Before loading network, summary.default is called, which produces a 
result that has names, and can be integrated in the global result of 
summary.data.frame. After loading network, summary.character is used 
instead, producing a result with a NULL name, hence the issue.

I think this qualifies as a bug, as loading the package changes the
behavior of a base function. Also, the change stays after detaching
the package, until R is restarted.

Is there any way to fix this?

Thanks a lot,

Matteo

messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] Weird summary behavior after loading the "network" package
messages.body_plain:
Hello again,

I found a turnaround this, by defining a function 
"format.summary.character" that restores the expected behavior of the 
code inside summary.data.frame. The function is inspired by format.factor:

format.summary.character <- function(x, ...) {
     s <- summary.default(as.character(x), ...)
     format(structure(as.character(s), names = names(s), dim = dim(s),
                      dimnames = dimnames(s)), ...)
}

After defining this function, the output of summary for character vector 
is still controlled by summary.character, but the output for 
summary.data.frame goes back to normal.

summary(test$a) # still calling summary.character

##   char   many   some vector   with  words
##      1      2      1      1      1      1

summary(test)   # back to normal

##       a                   b
##  Length:7           Min.   :1.0
##  Class :character   1st Qu.:2.5
##  Mode  :character   Median :4.0
##                     Mean   :4.0
##                     3rd Qu.:5.5
##                     Max.   :7.0
##

Hope it helps other users in the same situation.

Cheers,

Matteo

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Weird summary behavior after loading the "network" package
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] Weird summary behavior after loading the "network" package
messages.body_plain:
It's not a bug: the package happens to provide a summary method for a 
class that didn't already have one, and you just happen not to like how 
that method behaves.  This was implemented in the first place because 
yet other parties did not like how the default summary method treated 
character data (which was relevant to how the network package was being 
used), and wanted this behavior. Preferences can, and do, vary.

That said, I'm not personally wedded to this particular approach.  If 
enough folks dislike the current behavior, then we can take a look at 
modifying it in the future.

Hope that helps,

-Carter

Hello,

I'm having trouble fitting a model on my temporal data using the
relevent library. My call is:

rem.dyad(el, n=7, ordinal=F, effects=c("CovInt"),
covar=list(CovInt=hasT), hessian=T)

produces the following error:

Error in qr.solve(fit$hessian) : singular matrix 'a' in solve

Could someone point me in the right direction of why this is the case?
Could it be the case that this has to do with the type of data I use? I
have timestamped data of interactions which happen quite frequently in
short intervals, i.e. there might be 20 or more interactions in a minute
between the same nodes. I can aggregate these interactions over a
certain time window, no problem, if that's really the cause of the
error? Also, each observation has a Unix timestamp.

Thank you in advance,

Dear list members,

I am currently trying to infer dynamic networks that could explain the
spread of a given disease in general population.

I have a quite good quality egocentric dataset of individuals sexual
behavior, which I managed to fit quite well with a static network.

Now the challenge is to switch to dynamic ERGMs using stergm (and
potentially EpiModel) feqtures.

To be a bit more realistic, I would like to make my dissolution coefficient
dependant of the individual degree or just on the fact that an individual
has a concurrent relationship. The idea is to say that the probability of a
link to dissolve is more likely to happen for individuals having more than
one relationship at time.

For instance we could imagine that the average duration of a monogamous
relationship is 20 month and a concurent one 10 month. Then I tried to do
smth like:

dynfit<-stergm(sim.edges[[1]],
               formation = ~ edges ,
               dissolution = ~ offset(edges) + offset(concurrent),
               targets = "formation",
               target.stats = 240,
               offset.coef.diss = c(2.944, -0.747),
               estimate="EGMME",
               control = control.stergm(init.method = 'zeros'),
               eval.loglik = FALSE)

... Running this command make my computer fill-up all the memory until R
crash.. I never managed to make it converge so far.

First, am I allowed to do smth like that?
Is it the proper way to do it?

Does anybody have a smarter/more efficient way to do the job?

Bonus question: Is an equivalent in EpiModel via netest function exists?

I am more than happy to give you more info if required,

Best,
Damien
